text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Sports-only TV channel Sport 7 is to start insolvency proceedings this week. (p1)
- ABN Amrobank not able to directly carry out substantial number of EOE Options exchange orders last Friday due to order processing system breakdown. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm expects European finance ministers will close a stability pact on Thursday. (p1)
- Financial group Fortis finds no irregularities during inspection of books of MeesPierson, the bank it is to take over from ABN Amro. (p3)
- Retailer Ahold opens 16 shops under new BI-LO formula in Malaysia. (p3)
- KLM and unions of cabin staff to study necessity and dimension of the airline's economy drive Focus 2000. (p3)
- Consultancy bureau A.T.Kearney advises Campina Melkunie to shut two of its six dairy plants. (p3)
- Philips Electronics' new president Cor Boonstra tells inhouse magazine the company is still behind its competitors since launching reform programme Centurion in 1990. (p4)
- Merger between travel agencies Arke and Holland Int. in Travel Unie Int. Nederland will cost 77 jobs in the next three years. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Public broadcaster NOS stands big chance of getting back football rights from now bankrupt Sport 7. (p1)
- Dutch company Aduco gets French inventor's prize for its floating dam. (p2)
- Temp agency Randstad and unions row over wages for part- timers. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM cityhopper makes emergency landing at Heathrow airport London; one passenger lightly wounded. (p1)
- Eurocommissioner Hans van den Broek presses Dutch government to adjust drugs policy. (p3)
- Sport 7 insolvency application will not have a substantial influence of publisher De Telegraaf's 1996 profits. (p13)
TROUW
- Christian democrats CDA in parliament wants cabinet to adopt drugs policy to its European partners. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics and steel maker Hoogovens seek to sell their joint unit Amefo. (p11)
